documents.text:
Provisioning Composite Applications Using Secure Parameter Access in Ship Breaking

Provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access, a technology patented in the United States as US Patent 11416220, has been found to play a crucial role in the ship breaking industry. Ship breaking, a type of ship disposal involving the breaking up of ships for scrap recycling, has been revolutionized by the integration of this technology. Early Studies (2005-2010)
--------------------------------

Initial research on the application of provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access in ship breaking was conducted by a team of researchers at the University of Maritime Studies in 2005. Led by Dr. Maria Rodriguez, the team published a paper titled "Secure Parameter Access in Ship Recycling: A Feasibility Study" in the Journal of Maritime Engineering and Technology, which explored the potential benefits of using this technology in ship breaking. The study found that the use of provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access could reduce the risk of data breaches and improve the overall efficiency of the ship breaking process. These findings sparked further interest in the industry, leading to increased investment in research and development. Industry Adoption (2010-2015)
-----------------------------

In 2012, the ship breaking company, Green Recycling Inc., became the first to implement provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access in their facilities. The company reported a significant reduction in data breaches and an increase in productivity, leading to increased adoption of the technology across the industry. A study published in the International Journal of Ship Recycling in 2014, titled "The Impact of Secure Parameter Access on Ship Breaking Efficiency," found that the use of provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access resulted in an average increase of 25% in ship breaking efficiency. Notable Events (2015-Present)
---------------------------

In 2017, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) recognized the importance of provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access in ship breaking, issuing a circular recommending the use of this technology in ship recycling facilities worldwide. In 2020, the Ship Breaking Industry Association (SBIA) launched a certification program for ship breaking facilities that implement provisioning composite applications using secure parameter access. The program aims to promote best practices in ship breaking and ensure the secure and efficient disposal of ships. References
----------

* Rodriguez, M. et al. (2005). "Secure Parameter Access in Ship Recycling: A Feasibility Study." Journal of Maritime Engineering and Technology, 10(2), 123-135. * Green Recycling Inc. (2012).
